newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bakrie denies pressure to sell Indocopper.
newsitem.headline: Bakrie denies pressure to sell Indocopper.

text.p: Indonesian conglomerate Bakrie denied on Thursday it was under pressure from a group connected with President Suharto to sell its share of a firm with a stake in one of the world's biggest copper and gold producers.
"The sale is only a matter of timing. The deal is done at a fair price considering the market value," PT Bakrie & Brothers president director Tanri Abeng told reporters.
He said the firm was selling its 49 percent share of PT Indocopper Investama Corp, which has a stake in PT Freeport Indonesia, operator of the giant Grasberg mine in remote Irian Jaya province.
Tanri was responding to reporters' questions on why Bakrie & Brothers had decided to sell its shares in Indocopper, which owns 9.36 percent of Freeport, to Nusamba Mineral Industri.

Nusamba Mineral is part of the Nusamba Group, which is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto. Timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, who heads Nusamba, and Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto, each has a 10 percent stake.
Tanri said the firm had signed a Letter of Intent to sell its 49 percent Indocopper stake on Thursday to PT Nusamba Mineral Industri for $302.65 million.
Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States owns 81.28 percent of Freeport Indonesia, while the Indonesian government owns 9.36 percent of the firm.

Freeport McMoRan has a 49 percent stake in Indocopper, Bakrie & Brothers holds 49 percent before the sale, and Bakrie Group company Bakrie Investindo holds around 1.5 percent. The remaining shares are held by the public.
Tanri said Bakrie Investindo had also sold its stake in Indocopper to Nusamba. Investindo is not part of listed Bakrie & Brothers, but is part of the Bakrie Group.
Its financial results were not consolidated into Bakrie's results, he said. He gave no further details
Tanri said Bakrie & Brothers would finalise the sale only after gaining approval from an extraordinary shareholders' meeting expected to be held on March 12.
Bakrie's official announcement followed weeks of market talk of a possible sale, and denials by the firm.
Tanri said another party apart from Nusamba had expressed interest in buying Bakrie's stake in Indocopper but its offer was not as good as Nusamba's. He did not name the firm.
He said Bakrie had not negotiated directly with Nusamba and the deal had been arranged mainly through Bakrie's financial adviser, Salomon Brothers.
He said Nusamba had first expressed an interest in buying Bakrie's Indocopper stake late last year.
In reaching a decision, Bakrie had considered studies conducted by Salomon Brothers and investor relations services firm Forrest International, Tanri said.
Both had told Bakrie that divesting its Indocopper stake would make it structurally more attractive to investors and enhance its value, he said.
